title: DTree Explorer: Watching the Incremental Encoding of Directed Trees
description:
DTree Explorer shows the incremental encoding of directed trees by DTree at work. DTree places every node in two linear projections Q1 and Q2; node u reaches node v if and only if u precedes v in both, and inserting a node adds two positions without moving any other node. The Explorer builds a tree edge by edge and draws it in three views: the tree, the plane in which each node sits at its rank in Q1 and Q2, and the projections with the positions the library stores. Clicking nodes shows what reaches a node and what it reaches, and answers whether one node reaches another with both comparisons. Since version 1.3.0 the Explorer also shows EulerTree, which keeps Q1 alone with a closing cell for every node with children (the Euler tour), and lets the user choose rational or integer positions. The examples include those of the chapter "Topology and Structure of Directed Trees: An Incremental Encoding", among them the generalized insertion before or after a sibling (operators "s > c" and "s < c"). Every tree is computed by the published library triordinal-dtree (formerly dtree-encoding): locally with the installed package (pip install dtree-explorer), or in the browser with Pyodide.

Repository: https://github.com/EnisOlgac/DTree-Explorer. Install: pip install dtree-explorer, then dtree-explorer.
